elements.description: Structured rating of an answer: rubric scores, the failure type and the ideal answer, sent as one payload.

properties.name: answer
properties.description: The answer being rated – quoted at the top, and where the correction starts from

properties.name: criteria
properties.default: [ { id: "accuracy", label: "Accuracy", description: "Is everything it says true?" }, { id: "completeness", label: "Completeness", description: "Does it cover what was asked?" }, { id: "tone", label: "Tone", description: "Does it sound right for the reader?" }, ]
properties.description: The criteria, each scored on its own scale

properties.name: levels
properties.default: [ { value: 1, label: "Poor" }, { value: 2, label: "Weak" }, { value: 3, label: "Fair" }, { value: 4, label: "Good" }, { value: 5, label: "Excellent" }, ]
properties.description: The default scale for criteria without their own `levels`

properties.name: failureTypes
properties.default: [ { value: "hallucination", label: "Hallucination", description: "States something that isn't true or isn't in the sources" }, { value: "missing-context", label: "Missing context", description: "Didn't use something it was given or should have known" }, { value: "wrong-tone", label: "Wrong tone", description: "Too formal, too casual, or wrong for the reader" }, { value: "incomplete", label: "Incomplete", description: "Left part of the question unanswered" }, { value: "outdated", label: "Out of date", description: "Relies on something that is no longer true" }, { value: "formatting", label: "Formatting", description: "Hard to read: structure, length or layout" }, { value: "unsafe", label: "Unsafe", description: "Breaks a policy or could cause harm" }, ]
properties.description: The kinds of failure a person can pick, any number of them

properties.name: value
properties.description: The rating. Changed by the user unless a tc-value-change listener calls preventDefault()

properties.name: meta
properties.description: Sent along with the rating in tc-submit – ids and versions that tie it to the answer

properties.name: sent
properties.description: The rating was sent: the controls lock and "Edit rating" unlocks them. Set by Send; the app may set it too

properties.name: sending
properties.description: Shows Send as busy while the app saves the rating

properties.name: submitLabel
properties.description: The label on the send button

properties.name: payload
properties.description: The payload Send fires with tc-submit – the rating, the answer and `meta`

properties.name: look
properties.description: Visual style: "standard" or "clean"; unset follows <tc-look-provider>, else "standard"

events.name: tc-value-change
events.description: A score, a failure type or the correction changed ({ value }: FeedbackRubricValueChange); cancelable

events.name: tc-submit
events.description: Send was pressed with every required criterion scored (FeedbackRubricSubmit); cancelable – prevent it to stay editable

events.name: tc-edit
events.description: "Edit rating" unlocked a sent rating; no detail

props.name: title
props.description: The heading – defaults to "Rate this answer"

props.name: value
props.description: The rating. Controlled when defined; otherwise the component keeps it, starting from `defaultValue`

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The rating at first when `value` isn't controlled

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new rating after every score, failure type or correction edit, controlled or not

props.name: onSubmit
props.description:
Called when Send is pressed with every required criterion scored – the rating, the answer and `meta`. Return
false to keep the rubric editable

props.name: onEdit
props.description: Called when "Edit rating" unlocks a sent rating – set `sent` back to false if you control it

changelog: **Quality, retrieval, safety, structured output and conversation:** `tc-eval-scorecard`, `tc-feedback-rubric`, `tc-retrieval-inspector`, `tc-extraction-review`, `tc-guardrail-notice`, `tc-clarifying-questions`, `tc-structured-output`, `tc-generated-ui` and `tc-prompt-starters`.

features.name: light-dark()
features.why: Every colour token is a light / dark pair; without it no colour token resolves.

features.name: color-mix()
features.why: Tints and washes mixed from the tokens.

features.name: Container size queries
features.why: Components adapt to the width they're given, not the window's.

features.name: inert
features.why: Closed and leaving parts are out of the tab order and hidden from screen readers.

features.name: :has()
features.why: Layout and state that depend on what's inside a part (an icon present, a focused field).

features.name: :is() and :where()
features.why: Every rule is keyed on :where() so the page can override it.

features.name: field-sizing
features.without: Text fields grow with their text. Without it they keep their minimum height and scroll.

features.name: adoptedStyleSheets
features.without: Each element type's CSS goes into one <style> element in <head> instead – it looks and works the same.

features.name: forced-colors media query
features.without: In a forced-colours mode the browser's own adjustments apply, without the components' fixes.
